title: THE MORE THEY CRUSHED, THE MORE THEY GREW

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So they put slave masters over them to oppress them with forced labour, and they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh. But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites" - Exodus 1:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh's plan was logical. Break them with hard labour, and they will be too exhausted to grow. It failed completely. The more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied.

This is one of the great patterns of Scripture. What is meant to destroy God's people often becomes the very thing God uses to strengthen them. Joseph had already said it to his brothers: what you intended for evil, God intended for good. The early church saw the same thing — persecution scattered them, and the scattering spread the gospel further (Acts 8:4).

Be careful, though. This is not a promise that every hardship will feel productive or that pain is somehow good in itself. Slavery was real and brutal, and God calls it evil. The point is that God's purposes cannot be defeated by our enemies or by our circumstances.

The cross is the ultimate proof. The worst act in human history became the means of the world's salvation. If God can do that with a cross, He can do something with what is crushing you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I seen God bring growth out of a hard season?
2. Am I trusting God's purpose even when I cannot see it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You turned a cross into salvation. Do something redemptive with the pressure I am under, and keep my faith from breaking. Amen.
